notes.meaning: Jesus tells his disciples to stop letting their hearts be upset by the news that he is leaving. Even though hard trials and danger are coming, they do not need to panic. He urges them to put the same complete trust in him that they already place in God.

Jesus comforts his followers by picturing heaven as his Father's home with plenty of room for everyone. He is not abandoning them, but is going ahead to make a place ready for them through his death and return to glory. If there were no room for them, he would have told them so directly.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars suggest the word for rooms originally meant temporary resting places on a journey, or that the dwelling place refers to being joined with Christ rather than physical mansions in heaven.

notes.meaning: Jesus promises that after preparing their place, he will return to take them to be with him. The greatest joy of heaven is not golden streets, but living in direct fellowship with Jesus forever.

differ.view: Believe this verse specifically promises the rapture, where Christ comes in the air to take believers to heaven before a time of tribulation on earth.

notes.meaning: Jesus tells the disciples that they already know where he is going and how to get there. He had repeatedly explained that his destination was the Father and that the road led through his cross and resurrection.

Thomas speaks up with honest confusion, thinking Jesus was talking about a physical journey to an earthly place. Because the disciples still did not grasp that Jesus was returning to heaven, Thomas could not see what road they were supposed to take.

Jesus answers Thomas by declaring that he himself is the way, the truth, and the life. He does not merely point people toward God; he is the only path to the Father through his sacrifice and the living truth about God. No one can come into God's presence except through him.

Jesus explains that truly knowing him brings the true knowledge of God the Father. Because Jesus reveals God perfectly, the disciples have already begun to know and see the Father by walking with Jesus.

Philip asks Jesus to give them a visible sight of God, like the glorious visions granted to Moses and the prophets of old. He believes that seeing God directly with their own eyes would answer every question and settle their hearts.

Jesus gently corrects Philip for failing to understand him after years of walking together. Anyone who has seen Jesus has seen the Father, because Jesus is God living among humans. Looking for God outside of Jesus misses the one in whom God is fully present.
Jesus points out the complete unity between himself and the Father. His words are not merely his own human ideas, and his miracles are the Father actively working through him.

Jesus urges all the disciples to trust his claim that he and the Father share the same life and nature. If his words alone seem hard to grasp, they should at least look at the miracles he performed. Those mighty deeds provide undeniable proof of his divine power.

Jesus assures his followers that anyone who trusts in him will carry on his work. Because he is returning to the Father and sending his Spirit, his followers will see even greater results as the gospel spreads across the world.

differ.view: Believe the greater works include ongoing miraculous signs and physical healings performed through the power of the Holy Spirit.
Believe the greater works refer to the larger number of people converted through preaching the gospel worldwide, rather than more spectacular miracles.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Teaches that cooperating with God to bring about the spiritual salvation of souls is a greater work than physical miracles.

notes.meaning: Jesus promises to answer what his disciples pray in his name. Asking in his name means praying as his representatives, in harmony with his character and will. When Jesus answers such prayers, the Father receives honor through the Son.

Jesus repeats the promise to give his followers bold confidence in prayer. Even when people feel unworthy to approach God, they can bring their requests to Jesus, and he pledges to act on their behalf.

other.label: Popular modern teaching
other.view: Sometimes treats asking in Jesus' name like an automatic formula to receive whatever one desires, though mainstream teachers emphasize that it requires praying in alignment with God's will.

notes.meaning: Jesus shows that true affection for him is measured by obedience, not just emotional words. Loving Jesus means gladly following what he teaches and commands.

Jesus promises that he will ask the Father to send another Advocate—a helper and legal defender—to stay with believers forever. Just as Jesus had stood by them on earth, the Holy Spirit will now come alongside them as an unending helper.

This helper is the Spirit of truth, who teaches God's reality and protects believers from error. People focused only on worldly desires cannot receive him because they lack spiritual sight, but the disciples know him because he remains with them and will live inside them.

Jesus assures his followers that he will not abandon them like parentless children in a hostile world. Though he is about to die, he will come back to them soon through his resurrection and continuously by his Spirit.

Very soon the unbelieving world will see Jesus no more after he is buried, but his followers will see him alive again. Because Jesus conquers death and lives forever, believers have the sure guarantee that they will live with him too.

When Jesus rises and the Holy Spirit comes, the disciples will clearly understand the close bond between God and his people. They will recognize that Jesus is in the Father, that believers are joined to Jesus, and that Jesus lives within them.

The person who treasures Jesus' commands and puts them into practice is the one who truly loves him. The Father loves those who love his Son, and Jesus promises to reveal his presence and character clearly to every faithful disciple.

Judas, the apostle also known as Thaddaeus and not the traitor, asks why Jesus plans to reveal himself only to the disciples instead of displaying his power to the whole world. Like many people of his day, he expected the Messiah to set up an outward, public kingdom that everyone on earth could see.

Jesus explains that his kingdom comes as a quiet spiritual reality in the hearts of those who love and obey him. The Father loves the obedient believer, and both the Father and the Son will make an enduring home within that person's life.

Anyone who does not love Jesus refuses to follow his words. Disobeying Jesus is especially serious because his message does not originate with him alone, but comes straight from the Father who sent him.
Jesus reminds them that he has shared these truths while still physically living among them. Since his time on earth is short, he gives them these vital teachings to prepare them for what comes next.

Jesus promises that the Father will send the Holy Spirit in his name to serve as their personal teacher and guide. The Spirit will help the apostles understand all necessary truth and bring back to their memory everything Jesus had taught them.

Jesus leaves his disciples with peace, turning a common Jewish farewell greeting into a rich, permanent gift. The world offers only shallow, fragile peace based on circumstances, but Christ provides deep inner calm through reconciliation with God so his people need not be afraid.

Jesus tells the disciples that if they loved him with full understanding, they would rejoice that he is returning to the Father. Leaving his earthly weakness to regain his heavenly position beside the Father is a glorious step of honor for him and a blessing for them.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Teaches that the Father is greater in his role as the sender and source of the Son, while remaining entirely equal with the Son in divine essence and power.

notes.meaning: Jesus warns the disciples about his departure before it happens so that their faith will not be shattered. When they see every event unfold exactly as he said, their trust in him as God's Son will be firmly established.

Jesus explains that he will not talk with them much longer because Satan, the ruler of this fallen world, is advancing against him to bring about his arrest. Satan has no power or claim over Jesus, because Jesus is completely holy and free from sin.

Jesus goes to his death willingly so the entire world can see his perfect love and obedience to his Father's commands. He then tells his disciples to stand up and leave the upper room to face the coming trial together.
